previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman with Type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis s/p gastric pacer was readmitted three days after prior discharge for intractable nausea and vomiting. She presented with over 20 episodes of non-bloody, brown emesis and was found to have hypokalemia, hyponatremia, and sinus tachycardia. She was managed with NPO status, IV fluids, potassium repletion, and antiemetics including ondansetron, prochlorperazine, and lorazepam. Her blood pressure was controlled with IV metoprolol and transitioned to oral lisinopril. Gastric emptying study and upper GI with small bowel follow-through were normal, suggesting her symptoms were not due to motility or structural issues. Chronic microcytic anemia was identified, and iron supplementation was started. Due to recurrent symptoms without organic cause, outpatient brain MRI and psychiatric evaluation were recommended. Her diet was advanced to full, and she remained vomiting-free for two days prior to discharge. She was discharged home on her home medications with the addition of nightly lorazepam for nausea and anxiety.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female with history of T1DM with gastroparesis with 
recent normal gastric emptying study, who presents with severe 
nausea and vomiting.
  
#. Nausea/Vomiting: She presented with severe nausea and 
vomiting and inability to take oral intake.  She had a normal 
gastric emptying study on her last admission but it was felt 
that this likely did represent another episode of gastroparesis. 
 Central causes of nausea/vomiting were considered although she 
cannot have an MRI due to the gastric pacer.  Instead, she 
underwent CT head with contrast which showed no evidence of 
central process that may cause nausea and vomiting.  She was 
given IV fluids and kept NPO after admission.  She was continued 
on zofran, compazine, standing reglan, and ativan for nausea.  
Eventually her nausea resolved and her diet was advanced without 
complication.

#. T1DM: She had ketonuria on admission and developed a small 
anion gap with BS in the 300's.  Her home lantus was increased 
(from 28 to 31 units qhs) and her insulin sliding scale was 
increased by the ___ consult team.  Her blood sugar control 
improved.  She was discharged with her new sliding scale and 
instructed to follow-up with her PCP and endocrinologist.
  
#. HTN: She had hypertension to the 200's/90's on admission, 
thought to be secondary to vomiting/nausea and not being able to 
take her oral blood pressure medications.  She was given 
scheduled IV hydralazine to control her blood pressure which was 
eventually switched to her home lisinopril and IV metoprolol 
with improved control.  She was discharged on an increased dose 
of lisinopril and oral metoprolol as her hypertension continued 
even after her nausea and vomiting resolved.  She should have 
her blood pressure checked after discharge given her new doses 
and medications.

radiology_notes.text:
REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Vomiting.

PA and lateral upright chest radiographs were reviewed in comparison to ___.

The central venous line tip is at the level of mid low SVC.  Heart size is
normal.  Mediastinal position, contour and width are unremarkable.  Lungs are
essentially clear.  There is no pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  What
appears to be a pacemaker to the stomach due to gastroparesis is unchanged in
appearance.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with type 1 diabetes, gastroparesis, and
persistent nausea and vomiting.

TECHNIQUE:  Non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced CT images of the head were
obtained.  Intravenous contrast was administered.

COMPARISON:  CT of the head from ___ and sinus CT from ___.

FINDINGS:

There is an unchanged small lacune in the anterior limb of the right internal
capsule (series 3, image 11).
There is no evidence of intracranial masses, hemorrhage, edema, shift of
normally midline structures, or acute infarctions.  The ventricles and sulci
are normal in size and caliber.  No fractures or soft tissue abnormalities are
identified.  The paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear and well
aerated.

IMPRESSION:
1.  There is no evidence of intracranial masses, hemorrhage, or infarction.
2.  Unchanged small lacune in the anterior limb of the right internal capsule.
